items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: I said, “Hey Ginger, how you doing man, this is Chuck Lamb I’m a pianist and I’d doing a gig in Vail, I’d like you to come up and play, it’s a jazz gig.” And he goes, “How much does it pay?” And he came up.

ctx.x: Dan is quite an amazing guy. I remember here we are sitting on the stage that you all played on and I remember listening, at a couple of moments during that concert — I can’t remember if it was during a solo or what but I got this notion like I think Dan lost the beat. And boy was I wrong.

Well you know, I know what you mean. Yeah I’ve been playing with that cat for 20 years now and, you know, his “Take Five” solo, I mean his playing in general but his “Take Five” solo or his solos are just — I’m going man I’ve heard him do this now I don’t know how many thousands of times and I just shake my head standing there on the side of the stage. This dude is unreal. Nobody plays like that you know. I mean it’s almost like a rock — Ginger Baker hard hitting thing with like this mastery of time. You know you…

One part of doing what you do I believe is juggling commitments. Do you have — you have the Caffe Lena thing going and some lessons. Who takes precedence in your — is it the Brubecks that — they get on the calendar first?
